svg.title: Amazon EventBridge
svg.desc: Amazon EventBridge. An event bus: rules match events from AWS services, SaaS apps and your own code by content and route them to targets. Step 1, Where it sits: Your services, AWS and SaaS apps publish to buses; rules match events and route them to targets. Step 2, Rules match on content: PutEvents sends o-981 (1280) and o-982 (420): both match all-orders, only o-981 matches high-value. Step 3, Retries, DLQ and replay: Throttled target: retries for up to 1 h, then high-value-dlq. Replaying the archive fills analytics. Step 4, Limits and alternatives: At least once, no order: dedupe on orderId. Need order or retention? See the new Custom Event Bus.

g.text: Your services, AWS and SaaS apps publish to buses; rules match events and route them to targets.
PutEvents sends o-981 (1280) and o-982 (420): both match all-orders, only o-981 matches high-value.
Throttled target: retries for up to 1 h, then high-value-dlq. Replaying the archive fills analytics.
At least once, no order: dedupe on orderId. Need order or retention? See the new Custom Event Bus.
a copy of every shop-bus event
input transformer: Step Functions gets only
Your own services send events to a custom bus with PutEvents; AWS services publish to the default bus, SaaS partners to a partner bus.
A rule matches events by content and delivers them to up to 5 targets: Lambda, SQS, SNS, Step Functions, Kinesis, HTTPS APIs, other buses …
Producers publish facts, not commands: adding a consumer means adding a rule, with no change to the Orders service.
A pattern has the shape of the event, and every field it lists must match one of its values (prefix, suffix, anything-but, numeric, exists …).
o-981 is OrderPlaced, TH and 1280 ≥ 1000, so both rules match; o-982 fails the numeric test and only reaches analytics.
Every rule sees every event on its bus, and each match is a separate delivery. The archive keeps a copy of everything.
Retriable errors such as throttling are retried for 24 hours and up to 185 attempts by default; this target's RetryPolicy stops after 1 hour.
Then o-981 goes to the target's dead-letter queue, a standard SQS queue, with the error code; without a DLQ it would be dropped.
analytics went live today: a replay of the 24 hours before, sent only to all-orders, back-fills it. Replayed events carry replay-name.
LIMITS OF THE CLASSIC BUS · OCTOBER 2026
At least once and unordered: o-981 can arrive twice, and after o-982.
PutEvents: 10 entries and 1 MB per request · 10,000 requests/s in us-east-1 (adjustable).
Latency: P99 ≈ 130 ms to the first attempt (AWS, Aug 2024) · $1.00 per million custom events.
FIFO per event group, dedup; AWS's choice for new apps.
Pipes: one source → one target · Scheduler: rate, cron, at.
